RE: LD 503, SPO 221, An Act Regarding the Substance Use Services
Commission

Dear Senate Chair Senator lngwersen, Representative Chair Myer, and
members of the Joint Committee on Health and Human Services:

My name is Bruce Campbell and I serve as Chair of the Maine Substance Use Disorder Services Commission, established under MRS Title 5, Chapter 521 :
Subchapter 4A. The last time this statute was updated and approved by the
Governor was in June 2019. In the six years since, the Commission now
proposes amendments to that Act which reflect a more accurate description of
the Commission and its operations.

Attached is a summary of those changes as related to Membership; Meetings, compensation, quorum; and Duties of the commission. There are no substantive changes to the Commission, but these changes do reflect minor changes to these sections, in addition to the creation of a set of bylaws.
Specifically, these bylaws will address a change in operations that add Harm
Reduction to the continuum of care related to substance use disorders. In addition, it calls for separate subcommittees for each of the pillars or links to the continuum of care For substance use disorder services. In the alternate months of the Commission meetings, subcommittees representing prevention, intervention, harm reduction, treatment and recovety will meet separately to address specific concerns that would then be presented to the full
Commission. The subcommittee meetings will be recorded on zoom and minutes of the full Commission meeting will be recorded and distributed.
Attached is a summary of the proposed changes to the amendment. l am
willing to answer any questions.

Respectfully submitted,
Bruce A Campbell, LCSW, LADC
